fullPassage: Here's an application of metaphors to research papers: Below-grade-level readers in my urban middle school have a great deal of difficulty doing research. Their answer when assigned to do "a report" is to come to the media center and copy verbatim everything in the encyclopedia article or whatever source they have located, be it Internet, print, or whatever. To try to get the students to understand why it isn't necessary to copy everything in the articles, I use a comparison to a supermarket. I ask them if everything in the supermarket is useful, and we discuss this, with the usual conclusion being that it does, but we don't buy everything all the time. Then I ask them why they don't buy everything each time they go and how they determine what to buy when they go with their parents. Someone usually mentions that they have a list. From that point on, I lead a discussion about how whatever their teachers have asked for is their "shopping list" for their research, and they should just read for that information and write it down in note format. It sometimes helps them to understand that copying everything is a wasteful endeavor.

❌ ② 연구 과제의 어려움: 문제 제기일 뿐
❌ ③ 자료 신뢰성 비교: 원문에 없음
❌ ① 소비 교육: 슈퍼마켓은 비유일 뿐
det.tip: 주제 = 글쓴이가 전달하려는 핵심 메시지. 은유를 활용한 교육 방법.

questions.passage: Here's an application of metaphors to research papers: Below-grade-level readers in my urban middle school have a great deal of difficulty doing research. Their answer when assigned to do "a report" is to come to the media center and copy verbatim everything in the encyclopedia article or whatever source they have located, be it Internet, print, or whatever. To try to get the students to understand why it isn't necessary to copy everything in the articles, I use a comparison to a supermarket. I ask them if everything in the supermarket is useful, and we discuss this, with the usual conclusion being that it does, but we don't buy everything all the time. Then I ask them why they don't buy everything each time they go and how they determine what to buy when they go with their parents. Someone usually mentions that they have a list. From that point on, I lead a discussion about how whatever their teachers have asked for is their <u>"shopping list"</u> for their research, and they should just read for that information and write it down in note format.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "shopping list"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 연구에 필요한 정보의 범위를 정해주는 교사의 과제 요구사항
학생들이 매일 암기해야 할 단어 목록

det.korean: 쇼핑 목록 = 교사가 요구한 과제 사항, 즉 연구에서 찾아야 할 정보의 범위.
det.analysis:
❌ ② 실제 쇼핑 목록: 비유적 표현
✅ ① 교사의 과제 요구사항: shopping list는 연구에 필요한 정보 범위를 비유
❌ ③ 복사할 항목: 글의 논지는 '선별적' 수집
❌ ④ 암기할 단어: 원문에 없음
det.tip: 함축의미: shopping list(쇼핑 목록) = 연구 시 필요한 정보의 가이드. 비유적 표현.
